# Amatriciana

## Ingredients

- 150 g guanciale, cut into strips
- 400 g bucatini
- 400 g tinned tomatoes
- 1 small onion, finely sliced
- 60 g pecorino romano, grated
- a pinch of chilli flakes
- salt and olive oil

## Steps

1. Render the guanciale in a dry pan over medium heat until the fat runs and the strips are golden. Lift them out and set aside.
2. Soften the onion in the rendered fat, then add the chilli flakes.
3. Tip in the tomatoes, break them up, and simmer 20 minutes until the sauce thickens and darkens.
4. Boil the bucatini in well-salted water until al dente. Drain, keeping a little water.
5. Return the guanciale to the sauce, toss the pasta through with a splash of the water, then take it off the heat and stir in the pecorino romano.

## Troubleshooting

Sauce too thin means it needs more time uncovered, but keep the heat low or the tomatoes catch. Bitterness usually comes from scorched guanciale, so start it in a cold pan and watch it. Sauce that will not cling means too little starch, so save more cooking water. Cheese that seizes means the pan was too hot when the pecorino went in, so stir it in off the heat. The bucatini must stay firm or the whole dish turns to mush. If the sauce tastes flat, it usually needs another pinch of salt rather than more time. The guanciale should stay a little chewy in the middle, so pull it early and it finishes in the sauce.
